Elena —

Appreciate the redlines and the list. Quick answers upfront:

- Notification period: Redwood's standard is a 30-day published notice with the right to object within 30 days of notice. For large/regulatory-sensitive customers we can discuss an extended window on a case-by-case basis.
- Objection process: customer submits an objection to our Security & Privacy team; we evaluate mitigation and, if unresolved, escalate to an executive review. If a resolution cannot be reached we offer a documented workaround (e.g., tailored routing or use of an approved alternative processor).
- Execution: We use DocuSign for DPAs by default; Legal Ops will be the delegated signer on our side (Laura handles countersignature logistics).

I'm attaching a clean copy of our DPA with markup resolved (Redwood_DPA_Clean_v2.docx) and our current subprocessor snapshot. For timeline, I propose:

1) Redwood accepts a one-time compromise: we can extend the published-notice period to 45 days for NimbusPay for processors marked as "critical" on both lists.
2) Objection window remains 30 days from notice.
3) Execution via DocuSign; Laura will send envelope once both sides sign off on the DPA text.

If that sounds acceptable, we'll put together a short action plan and Laura will send the envelope.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Elena —

Couple of clarifying points from legal review:

1) Snapshot vs rolling list: Redwood publishes a canonical subprocessor registry (public URL); notices are triggered when a new processor is added or when an existing processor's role materially changes. The registry is the source of truth; the execution snapshot will be captured at signature but does not limit subsequent additions that follow the notice process.

2) Notice windows: we proposed 45 days for critical processors as a compromise. If NimbusPay requires 90 days we need a clear list of which processors you'd consider "critical" and why — in many cases customers accept shorter windows if they have a fast internal review path.

3) Data transfers: we will rely on standard SCCs for EU transfers and our contractual transfer mechanisms for other regions. If NimbusPay requires local hosting or special cross-border constraints, we should capture that in an annex.

Laura, can you confirm you can prepare the DocuSign envelope and include a clause that defines the public subprocessor registry URL in the DPA?

Thanks,
